text:
Alex: FYI Priya opened an escalation — p95/p99 tail latency regressions after enabling int8 quantization on their Dedicated deployment. They flipped the quant profile and saw big tail increases plus a couple of odd tokens.

Alex: Customer reported numbers: BEFORE: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~380ms. AFTER int8 aggressive: p95 ~470ms, p99 ~1.2s, occasional token glitches on sampling.

Alex: Their minimal repro:
```
POST /v1/deployments/dep-xyz789/config
{ "quantization": "int8", "profile": "aggressive" }
# then run 4 concurrent streams, seq_len=1024, nuclear sampling
```

Sam: can you attach their trace/flamegraph here? need kernel selection logs and any fallback markers.

Alex: attached trace snippets:
```
[trace] id=abc stage=compile kernel=matmul_int8 fallback=matmul_fp16 reason=overflow
[trace] id=abc latency=1200ms stage=attention kernel_select=hybrid
```

Maya: that pattern screams quant-calibration overflow -> runtime switching to fp16 fallback mid-request. Fallback incurs memcpy + dequant/requant steps and loses fused kernels => big tail. Also explains token diffs.

Jordan: infra check: no GPU throttles, memory stable, autoscale fine. Routing OK. I'll pull kernel logs for past 24h.

Sam: model flavor? some architectures are very sensitive to int8 per-head scales and rotary embeddings.

Alex: model is rwd-2-large-vector, supports 16k context, custom tokenizer.

Maya: actionable repro for us:
- run quant-calibrate using customer's sample corpus
- inspect per-layer scale/zero histograms, watch for extreme zps
- run forced int8 kernels (`--force-kernel=int8`) to see deterministic failures

Maya: short mitigation for customer: revert to `fp16` or use a conservative `int8-safe` profile. Also they can add per-request header to override quant without redeploy: `X-Redwood-Quant: fp16`.

Sam: revert API example for them:
```
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deployments/dep-xyz789/config\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"quantization":"fp16","profile":"default"}'
```
Note: config roll typically ~30s-2m; can add `?force_rolling=true` to expedite.

Alex: is `X-Redwood-Quant` supported on Dedicated?

Sam: yes on dedicated >= v2.11.0 — it forces per-request runtime path without re-deploy. Good for quick mitigation.

Priya: trying header now, will report p95/p99. Uploading 6 representative prompts (short + long). :crossed_fingers: 

ops-bot: deploybot: config change queued for dep-xyz789 (api request) — est apply 52s

Priya: header applied, p95 dropped to ~190ms in under a minute. p99 trending down too.

Maya: when you upload samples, include prompts that stress long context and those that touch safety filters. I'll run:
```
quant-calibrate --corpus sample.jsonl --model rwd-2-large-vector --out safe_profile.json
```
I'll examine per-layer histograms and report any layers with high overflow probability.

Sam: interim engineering options to discuss:
- make fallback path cheaper (reduce copies or do on-device format conversion)
- add console preflight that simulates calibration on small sample before enabling aggressive int8
- implement traffic-split canary with auto-rollback on tail latencies

Maya: longer term: add per-head clipping heuristics and per-layer thresholding, and a lightweight online calibrator to avoid cold-run overflows. Also consider exposing an `int8-safety-score` in the Console.

Alex: immediate action list: (1) I’ll send the revert/recommendation to customer + ask for 5-10 prompts (ETA 1h) (2) Maya will run offline calibration and produce a `safe_int8` profile (ETA 4h) (3) Jordan will gather kernel selection logs for last 24h and attach to ticket (ETA 2h).

Priya: uploaded samples. thanks everyone. switching back to fp16 header for production.

Jordan: logs collected and attached to ticket. I can see repeated `overflow` markers aligning with customer spikes.

Maya: running calibration now. preliminary: two transformer layers show outlier scales; aggressive profile clips them too harshly causing numeric instability. I can generate a profile that avoids those clip thresholds.

Alex: draft customer reply: "Thanks Priya — for immediate relief set header `X-Redwood-Quant: fp16` or run the curl revert. We got your samples; well produce a conservative int8 profile and share. Will update in ~4h."

Sam: note for cost talk: int8 saves memory and can lower unit cost, but if the runtime frequently falls back to fp16 you pay both overhead and worse tails. Recommend conservative profile + offline calibration to actually get cost wins.

Maya: I'll also simulate warm vs cold runs at different concurrencies to measure overflow probability. Will post numbers.

Alex: closing loop with Priya now. tagging eng for follow-ups and RFC for a Console preflight check. thanks team. :pray:
